findings.title: Light-theme lightness of embedded-post username link unintentionally changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The mechanical dark-theme conversion used everywhere else in this PR keeps the `$primary` lightness argument unchanged and only adds a complementary `$secondary` branch. Here the `$primary` branch was changed to `$lightness: 70%`, so light themes now render the username link in embedded/in-reply-to posts much lighter than before, while the intended fix was only about dark themes. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: .custom-message-length light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness, diverging from desktop
findings.body: The rule `.custom-message-length` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The PR changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, altering the light-theme value (30% instead of 70%) — every other conversion in this PR preserves the `$primary` lightness. The equivalent desktop rule in `desktop/modal.scss` was correctly converted to 70%/30%, so mobile and desktop now disagree and mobile light themes get a much darker character-counter color. It should be 70%/30%.

findings.title: .topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%, altering light-theme rendering
findings.body: In the mobile topic map, `h3` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Both the light value (20% → 50%) and the dark value (expected complement 80%, got 50%) were changed, so light themes get a lighter map heading and dark themes get a less-contrast heading than the intended conversion. The desktop counterpart (`desktop/topic-post.scss` .topic-map h3) correctly uses 20%/80%, so mobile is now inconsistent with desktop for the same element.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% in both theme branches
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The `$primary` lightness should have stayed 30% (with a 70% complement for `$secondary`), so light-theme group member names are now lighter than before, and the dark-theme value is not the complement of the original. Compare with the sibling `.username a` rules elsewhere which correctly keep 30%/70%.

findings.title: Same 30%→50% lightness regression in mobile group-member-info .name
findings.body: In `mobile/user.scss`, `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. As with the desktop copy, the `$primary` lightness should have remained 30% (dark branch 70%), so light-theme rendering changes unintentionally and the dark value is not the complement. This mirrors the desktop/user.scss error and should be 30%/70%.

findings.title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still scales only $primary
findings.body: This PR converts every `scale-color($primary, ...)` color to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, ...), scale-color($secondary, ...))` so it works on dark themes, but `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification { color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%); }` in the same file was left untouched. On a dark color scheme (where `$primary` is light), scaling `$primary` toward 50% lightness produces a mid-gray that is the same pattern this PR exists to fix, so this instance looks like an oversight rather than an intentional exclusion — the adjacent `th`/`td` rules in the same file were converted.
